newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS -- U.S. propane rally still full of steam.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS -- U.S. propane rally still full of steam.

text.p: The rally in U.S. propane prices is expected to stretch into December as cold temperatures continue to drive demand and keep alive concerns over low inventories, analysts said.

"It's a hypersensitive market right now. For the next three months every time there is a forecast for a new blast of cold weather prices will go up," said Ron Gist, an analyst with Purvin and Gertz who follows liquified petroleum gases.
Gist said he expects the current rally to be a see-saw with prices peaking out in January.

The primary factor behind the surge in prices has been the early arrival of freezing temperatures in the central and northeastern parts of the U.S., which quickly brought retailers to the table to buy before prices rose any further.
"A lot of the end-users have been holding back expecting prices would drop but now basically they have to belly up to the bar and buy supplies at any cost," said Gist.
In the past week traders have reported a number of small 2,500-barrel parcels being sold to retailers in the Midwest supplying the rural home heating market.
Farmers pulling in the last of their corn crops have also been drawing hard on the propane pool to beat the arrival of frost.
"There has been a high demand for crop drying but the primary factor is the weather," said Gist.
Prices all year have been higher than usual due to low inventories, depleted by last year's harsh winter and strong petrochemical demand .
Analysts said spot November propane prices are expected to average 55.00 cents a gallon, about 75 percent above the four-year historical average of 31.40 cents.
